normal.text: "$200? Best I can do is two old games and a mid-tier controller."

normal.name: James Irish
normal.text: It's funny. The only time PC gaming ever ruined a console experience for me was when Resident Evil came out. I was spoiled rotten by Lucasarts games like Day of the Tentacle and Sam & Max Hit the Road. When I heard those old RE1 voice actors, I was a little incredulous.

normal.name: Koopoko (Dokoro, Doko, etc.)
normal.text: Re-ran the game with Leon A on the modded Steam PC version (HD pack + convenience features added in like quick turn). Did quite well this time for only my first try of Leon A.

normal.name: Two Thangs: pop art supreme
normal.text: A classic! It's the Futurama / NES painting that was featuring only the classic and original Nintendo Entertainment System. You know what that came with? Super Mario Brothers! You know you got down with your friends playing that one and falling into a pit over and over.

normal.name: Emily the Goblingirl 🏳️‍⚧️
normal.text: Does it have a talking cat? Because that was the thing that won me over for DCC. I am a sucker for talking cats. With attitude. Also it was my first encounter with the whole leveling up it’s a video game in a book kind of thing. Which was fun.

normal.name: Umni
normal.text: backloggd.com/u/_umni_/rev... #Backloggd #N64 This was a really fun throwback. When I was a kid remember feeling like the DK world was so massive. I would just walk around DK Isle just for the fun of it. I wish Nintendo would bring back the other Kongs, they’re so much fun to play as.

normal.text: A thought I've been kicking around for awhile and a sentiment I hold personally is that as fun as it is to see the old games we grew up with refreshed and brought to the modern day, realistically we just want to see those world expanded further by the very people who concieved them to begin with.
